title: How many ants reach each food source?
description: A colony of ants splits equally four times and reaches a mango tree and a sugarcane field. The fraction of the group at each split is found by multiplying, and the shares at each food source are added over a common denominator.
teaching_notes: One idea: follow the group split by split, multiplying to find each share, then add the shares that end at the same place. Watch for students who add the shares without a common denominator, or who forget the part that goes on to the next split.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): a colony of ants set out in search of food. As they search, they keep splitting equally at each point and reach two food sources, one near a mango tree and another near a sugarcane field. What fraction of the original group reached each food source?
video_script.why: A learner follows a group through equal splits, multiplying fractions of fractions as with the red square, and then adds the shares that end in the same place.
video_script.substitution: the book's own ants that split equally four times on the way to a mango tree and a sugarcane field
video_script.anchor: a path of ants that splits four times, with a mango tree and a sugarcane field at the ends
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty nine thirty seconds reached the mango tree, and three thirty seconds reached the sugarcane field.

final_answer.value: 29/32 reached the mango tree and 3/32 reached the sugarcane field
final_answer.spoken: twenty nine thirty seconds reached the mango tree, and three thirty seconds reached the sugarcane field

video_script.fraction_reading: half, one quarter, one sixteenth, two sixteenths, one thirty second, twenty nine thirty seconds, three thirty seconds
maths_rules: split 1: 1/2 reaches the mango tree and 1/2 goes on
split 2: 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4 reaches the mango tree and 1/4 goes on
split 3: 1/4 ÷ 4 = 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16 for each part; two parts reach the mango tree, one reaches the sugarcane field, 1/16 goes on
split 4: 1/16 ÷ 2 = 1/16 x 1/2 = 1/32 for each food source
video_script.design: A branching path drawn once, with the fraction of the group written on each branch as it is found; the working band adds the branches that end at the same food source.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a line of ants at the start of a branching path, a mango tree and a sugarcane field at the ends

marks.ask: the mango tree and the sugarcane field light up

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a colony of ants.
The ants set out in search of food.
<bookmark mark='food'/>They keep splitting into equal groups along the way.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>At the end, they reach a mango tree and a sugarcane field.
What fraction of the original group reached each food source?

beats.on_screen: the branching path stays on the board; Keeko sits beside it

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the path drawn with its four splits; each split labelled with where the ants go

marks.first: the first split sends half to the mango tree and half upwards
marks.second: the second split sends half of that group to the mango tree and half upwards
marks.third: the third split makes four equal parts
marks.last: the last split sends half to each food source

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>At the first split, half the ants go to the mango tree and half go upwards.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second split sends half of that group to the mango tree and half upwards.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third split makes four equal parts.
Two go to the mango tree, one goes to the sugarcane field, and one goes upwards.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last split sends half to the mango tree and half to the sugarcane field.

beats.on_screen: Given: the group splits equally 4 times; the ants end at a mango tree and a sugarcane field

marks.given: the four splits and the two food sources are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a group of ants splits equally four times.
They end at a mango tree and a sugarcane field.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fraction of the original group at each food source

marks.find: the words each food source are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the fraction of the original group at each food source.

beats.on_screen: split 1: 1/2 to the mango tree, 1/2 goes on;  split 2: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 to the mango tree, 1/4 goes on

marks.one: half is written at the mango branch of the first split
marks.two: half of the half is written at the second split
marks.mult: half times half gives one quarter, which goes on

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, at the first split, half reach the mango tree and half go on.
<bookmark mark='two'/>At the second split, half of that half reach the mango tree.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Half times half is one quarter, and one quarter goes on.

beats.on_screen: split 3: 1/4 ÷ 4 = 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16 for each part;  2 parts to the mango tree, 1 part to the sugarcane field, 1/16 goes on

marks.third: the one quarter is cut into four equal parts
marks.each: one quarter divided by four becomes one quarter times one quarter
marks.parts: two parts go to the mango tree, one to the sugarcane field, and one goes on

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step two, the third split cuts the one quarter into four equal parts.
<bookmark mark='each'/>Each part is one quarter divided by four, which is one quarter times one quarter.
That is one sixteenth.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Two parts reach the mango tree, one reaches the sugarcane field, and one sixteenth goes on.

marks.last: the one sixteenth is shared between the two food sources
marks.each: one sixteenth times a half gives one thirty second each

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step three, the last split shares the one sixteenth between the two food sources.
<bookmark mark='each'/>Each gets one sixteenth times a half, which is one thirty second.

marks.mango: the four shares at the mango tree are written
marks.same: each share is written over thirty two
marks.sum: the numerators are added over thirty two

narration: <bookmark mark='mango'/>Step four, add what reached the mango tree.
Half plus one quarter plus two sixteenths plus one thirty second.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Write each as thirty seconds, which gives sixteen, eight, four and one.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Add the numerators, sixteen plus eight plus four plus one, over thirty two.

marks.sugar: the two shares at the sugarcane field are written
marks.same: one sixteenth becomes two thirty seconds and the numerators are added over thirty two

narration: <bookmark mark='sugar'/>Step five, add what reached the sugarcane field.
One sixteenth plus one thirty second.
<bookmark mark='same'/>One sixteenth is two thirty seconds, so add the numerators, two plus one, over thirty two.

beats.on_screen: check: mango tree part + sugarcane field part = the whole group
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check that the two parts together make the whole group.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 29/32 reached the mango tree and 3/32 reached the sugarcane field.  Check: 29/32 + 3/32 = 32/32 = 1

marks.ans: both answers are boxed at their food sources
marks.check: the two parts are added to give one whole

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Twenty nine thirty seconds reached the mango tree, and three thirty seconds reached the sugarcane field.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Twenty nine plus three is thirty two.
The two parts make thirty two over thirty two, the whole group.
